description: An intellectual debut within the halls of the ancient Academy. Test your strength in searching for the fundamental terms of science and philosophy.

words.DOGMATISM: A way of thinking that operates with unalterable concepts and excludes critical analysis.
words.HYPOTHESIS: A scientific assumption put forward to explain a phenomenon and requiring verification.
words.AXIOM: A statement accepted without logical proof due to its inherent truth.
words.THEOREM: A mathematical statement, the truth of which is established by means of a proof.
words.ANALYSIS: A research method that breaks down the studied object into its constituent parts.
words.SYNTHESIS: The combination of various elements into a single whole in the process of cognition.
words.DIALECTICS: A philosophical method of argumentation that investigates the internal contradictions of phenomena.
words.LOGIC: The science of the laws, forms, and methods of correct thinking.
words.SOPHISM: A formal, seemingly correct, but inherently false argument or conclusion.

description: A gaze through telescope lenses into the depths of space. The words of this level describe the grandiose phenomena of the Universe.

words.ASTEROID: A small celestial body of the Solar System moving in an orbit around the Sun.
words.GALAXY: A giant, gravitationally bound system consisting of stars, gas, dust, and dark matter.
words.SUPERNOVA: A phenomenal astronomical event accompanied by a colossal explosion of a star.
words.QUASAR: An extragalactic object of high luminosity powered by a supermassive black hole.
words.ORBIT: The path of a celestial body or an artificial spacecraft in the gravitational field of another body.
words.ZENITH: The highest imaginary point of the celestial sphere located directly above the observer's head.
words.INTERIOR: The inner depths of a cosmic body hidden from direct observation.
words.TELESCOPE: An optical instrument for observing distant astronomical objects.
words.PULSAR: A rotating neutron star that emits strictly periodic pulses of radiation.

description: Labyrinths of myths and ancient civilizations. Unravel the terms that are rooted in antique culture.

words.ARCHETYPE: A universal innate psychic prototype that structures human perception.
words.PANTHEON: A collection of gods of a particular religion, or a monumental building dedicated to them.
words.ARTIFACT: An object of material culture created or modified by a human in the past.
words.ALLEGORY: A artistic personification of abstract concepts through concrete images.
words.LABYRINTH: A complex structure with many tangled paths and dead ends.
words.MYTHOLOGY: A system of tales about gods, heroes, and the origin of the universe.
words.RITUAL: A traditional order of performing solemn or religious actions.
words.TOTEM: A symbolic animal or plant considered an ancestor and protector of a clan.
words.LEGEND: A poetic tradition or story about a historical event or personality.

description: An era of great discoveries and complex mechanisms. A level for connoisseurs of exact sciences and inventions.

words.CAPACITOR: An electronic two-terminal component designed to store an electrical charge.
words.RESONANCE: The phenomenon of a sharp increase in the amplitude of oscillations when frequencies match.
words.ALCHEMY: A pre-scientific direction in chemistry that sought to obtain the philosopher's stone.
words.TRAJECTORY: A continuous line described by a material point during its movement.
words.MECHANISM: A system of links designed to convert the motion of one body into the motion of others.
words.DYNAMICS: A branch of mechanics that studies the motion of bodies under the action of applied forces.
words.MOMENTUM: A vector physical quantity that serves as a measure of mechanical motion.
words.ENERGY: A scalar physical quantity that is a unified measure of various forms of motion.
words.THERMOSTAT: A device for maintaining a constant temperature in an enclosed space.

description: The final exam in the Royal Library. Words for true erudites who master the language masterfully.

words.VESTIGE: An organ or trait that has lost its primary significance in the course of evolution.
words.ECLECTICISM: An artistic mixing or combination of heterogeneous styles, ideas, or views.
words.METAMORPHOSIS: A complete, radical change of form, structure, or inner essence.
words.SYNECDOCHE: A trope, a stylistic device based on transferring meaning from a part to the whole.
words.METAPHOR: A figure of speech consisting in the use of a word or expression in a figurative meaning.
words.PARADOX: A situation that can exist in reality but has no logical explanation.
words.GENOTYPE: The sum total of all genes localized in the chromosomes of a given organism.
words.RETROSPECTIVE: A look into the past, an examination of past events or stages of development.
words.PHENOMENON: An unusual occurrence, a rare fact, something that is difficult to understand or explain.
